sn45.160:1.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, that when the river Ganges slants, slopes, and inclines towards the east,
sn45.160:1.2: a great crowd of people would come along bringing a shovel and a basket, thinking:
sn45.160:1.3: ‘We will make this river Ganges slant, slope, and incline towards the west.’
sn45.160:1.5: would that great crowd of people be able to make the river Ganges slant, slope, and incline towards the west?”
sn45.160:1.8: Because the river Ganges slants, slopes, and inclines towards the east,
sn45.160:1.9: and it is not easy to make it slant, slope, and incline towards the west.
sn45.160:1.10: That great crowd of people would only reap fatigue and vexation.”
sn45.160:1.11: “So too, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is developing and cultivating the Noble Eightfold Path, kings or royal ministers, friends or colleagues, relatives or kinsmen, might invite him to accept wealth, saying:
sn45.160:1.12: ‘Come, good man, why let these saffron robes weigh you down?
sn45.160:1.13: Why roam around with a shaven head and a begging bowl?
sn45.160:1.14: Come, having returned to the lower life, enjoy wealth and do meritorious deeds.’
sn45.160:1.15: Indeed, bhikkhus, when that bhikkhu is developing and cultivating the Noble Eightfold Path, it is impossible that he will give up the training and return to the lower life.
sn45.160:1.17: Because for a long time his mind has slanted, sloped, and inclined towards seclusion. Thus it is impossible that he will return to the lower life.
sn45.160:1.18: “And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu develop and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path?
sn45.160:1.19: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view … right concentration, which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, maturing in release.
sn45.160:1.20: It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path.”
